title: Modernise the clearing batch: COBOL to Rust
summary: Port a legacy COBOL program to Rust, proved equivalent by a tool against the live COBOL
story: The nightly clearing batch, CLEARING.cbl, totals each night's settlement records by scheme; its totals feed the settlement reconciliation. Its runtime reaches end of life on 31 December 2026 and its last maintainer retires in September, so it must be ported, with proof that nothing changed.

card.about: A legacy modernisation done the way a regulated bank must do it. A tool computes the program's record and report layouts from its own source; NexCODE ports the logic to Rust with the Bank's COBOL compatibility crate, guided by the four layers of rules; and a tool proves the port equivalent by running the real COBOL beside it on the same fixture and comparing the two reports byte for byte. The evidence record carries that proof.
card.scenario: Priya Nair picks up MOD-2026-07. The clearing batch must leave its end-of-life COBOL runtime, and the 2024 rewrite of a fee batch (PM-2024-011) went live without proof and lost pennies for nine weeks. Select runs the real COBOL on the fixture first; the migration step asks NexCODE for the Rust port and its characterisation test; the presenter applies them and runs the tests, which compile the port, run it, compare its report with the COBOL's and run the test.

steps.title: Migrate to Rust
steps.prompt: Migrate nexus-payments/legacy/clearing-batch/CLEARING.cbl to Rust (MOD-2026-07, its Rust variant, which Marcus Thorne agreed under ADR-008 D2). Keep its behaviour identical: the same input must give the same report, byte for byte. Write nexus-payments/services/clearing-rs/Cargo.toml (package `clearing`, edition 2021, depending only on `cobol-compat = { path = "../../libs/cobol-compat-rs" }`), nexus-payments/services/clearing-rs/src/main.rs, taking the input file and the report file as its two arguments, and the characterisation test nexus-payments/services/clearing-rs/tests/characterisation.rs, which runs the program (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_clearing")) on legacy/clearing-batch/clearing_input.dat and compares its report with legacy/clearing-batch/expected_totals.txt by cobol_compat::report::assert_same_bytes(expected, actual), building both paths from env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") (the repository root is two folders up) and writing its report under std::env::temp_dir(). Use the Bank's COBOL compatibility crate (cobol_compat) as MIG-005 requires, and do not write your own versions of it: fixed_record::text and fixed_record::decimal for each input field, Fixed for every amount, cobol_math::rounded for COMPUTE ... ROUNDED, picture::edit and picture::edit_count for every edited picture, picture::text for every text item moved into a report line, line_sequential to read the input and write the report, and report::assert_same_bytes to compare the two reports in the test. Pass each PICTURE exactly as the COBOL source writes it, with its column from the layouts.

repair.prompt: The tests failed: the attached run shows which check failed. Fix the port so its report is identical to the COBOL's, byte for byte, and its characterisation test passes; give each changed file whole again.

talkTrack: Mature estates carry exactly this burden. Select the demo: the real COBOL compiles and runs on the fixture, and its report matches the expected one. Migrate: a tool lays out the program's records, NexCODE ports the logic to Rust with the Bank's compatibility crate and writes the characterisation test. Apply and run the tests: the port's report is compared with the COBOL's, byte for byte, by a tool. Record: the proof goes into the evidence record.
